parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Potassium combines with sulfur to form an ionic compound, potassium sulfide, K 2 S.

ms.label: 2(b)(i)
ms.text:
any two (one from each bullet point)
•
physical constants: high boiling point / melting point
•
conductivity: conduct electricity when aqueous / conduct electricity when molten
•
solubility: soluble in water

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Complete the dot-and-cross diagram to show the electron arrangement and charges of the ions in potassium sulfide. [3]

ms.label: 2(b)(ii)
ms.text:
M1 eight dots in third shell of both K (1)
M2 six crosses and two dots in third shell of S (1)
M3 ‘+’ charge on each K on correct answer line and ‘2–‘ charge on S ion on correct answer line (1)

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) When potassium is added to water, it reacts vigorously and a coloured flame is seen. The equation for the reaction is shown. 2K(s) + 2H 2 O(l) → 2KOH(aq) + H 2 (g)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The solution formed is potassium hydroxide, a strong alkali. State the formula of the ion responsible for alkalinity in a solution. ....................................................................................................................................... [1]

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate the volume, in cm 3 , of hydrogen gas formed when 2.34 g of potassium is added to excess water at room temperature and pressure. Use the following steps. ● Calculate the number of moles of potassium added. = .............................. mol ● Determine the number of moles of hydrogen gas formed. = .............................. mol ● Calculate the volume of hydrogen gas formed. volume = .............................. cm 3 [3]
